fullPassage: The young Jacques Monod in 1941 was curious about the factors influencing the growth of a colony of bacteria when he noticed something he did not understand. He knew that when the food supply contained only one kind of sugar, the growth rate of the colony of bacteria was linear. When he fed the bacteria two different sugars, there was a brief pause in the growth rate before the expected linear increase. Monod's pursuit of the reason for the puzzling pause in growth rate led to a discovery that won him a Nobel Prize. A fair proportion of psychologists are more interested in proving the validity of a favorite idea rather than probing a puzzling observation. Individuals vary in the frequency of bouts of depression. A biologist is likely to focus on this variation and try to discover all the responsible conditions. Psychologists more often select one particular cause - say, loneliness - and try to prove that this condition can bring on a depression. This strategy ignores the possibility that those who are depressed possess a biology and life history that predate both the loneliness and the depression. An overweight, unattractive woman with no close friends who grew up in poverty, dropped out of high school, and cannot get a good job is susceptible to a metabolic illness, which can cause a bout of depression. Although she might tell a psychologist that she feels lonely, this feeling may not be the major cause of her melancholic mood.

When he fed the bacteria two different sugars, there was a brief pause in the growth rate before the expected linear increase. Monod's pursuit of the reason for the puzzling pause in growth rate led to a discovery that won him a Nobel Prize. A fair proportion of psychologists are more interested in proving the validity of a favorite idea rather than probing a puzzling observation. Individuals vary in the frequency of bouts of depression. A biologist is likely to focus on this variation and try to discover all the responsible conditions. Psychologists more often select one particular cause - say, loneliness - and try to prove that this condition can bring on a depression. This strategy ignores the possibility that those who are depressed possess a biology and life history that predate both the loneliness and the depression. An overweight, unattractive woman with no close friends who grew up in poverty, dropped out of high school, and cannot get a good job is susceptible to a metabolic illness, which can cause a bout of depression. Although she might tell a psychologist that she feels lonely, this feeling may not be the <u>major</u> cause of her melancholic mood.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 major의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: major(주요한, 주된) ↔ minor(사소한, 부차적인)
det.analysis:
❌ ① chief — 주된 (동의어)
✅ ② minor — 사소한, 부차적인 (반의어) ←정답
❌ ③ final — 마지막의 (의미축 다름)
❌ ④ royal — 왕의 (의미축 다름)

questions.passage:
(A) Psychologists more often select one particular <u>cause</u>, such as loneliness, and try to prove that it brings on a depression.

(B) Heavy rain and melting snow can <u>cause</u> a serious flood in the valley within a few hours.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 cause의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 하나의 특정 '원인'(명사) / (B) ~을 '유발하다, 초래하다'(동사)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 원인 — 유발하다 ←정답
❌ ② 원인 — 원인 (B는 동사 '유발하다')
❌ ③ 대의명분 — 유발하다 (A는 '대의'가 아니라 '원인')
❌ ④ 원인 — 소송 (B는 '소송'이 아니라 '유발하다')

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어는?

"a scientist who studies living organisms such as animals and plants"

det.korean: 동물과 식물 같은 살아 있는 생물을 연구하는 과학자 → biologist(생물학자)
det.analysis:
❌ ① psychologist — 심리학자 (마음·행동 연구)
❌ ② chemist — 화학자 (물질 연구)
❌ ③ physicist — 물리학자 (물질·에너지 연구)
✅ ④ biologist — 생물학자 ←정답

questions.passage: The young Jacques Monod in 1941 was curious about the factors __________ (influence) the growth of a colony of bacteria when he noticed something he did not understand.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 명사 the factors를 뒤에서 꾸미는 현재분사 형태가 필요하다 → influence → influencing
det.analysis: the factors __________ (influence) the growth → 앞의 명사 factors를 수식하는 현재분사(능동, ~하는) 자리 → influencing
det.tip: 명사를 뒤에서 수식하는 현재분사: influence → influencing

questions.passage: Psychologists more often select one particular cause - say, loneliness - and try to prove that this condition can bring on a depression. This strategy ignores the possibility that those who are __________ (depress) possess a biology and life history that predate both the loneliness and the depression.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: be동사 are 뒤에서 '우울한' 상태를 나타내는 과거분사(수동)가 필요하다 → depress → depressed
det.analysis: those who are __________ (depress) → be동사(are) 뒤 과거분사 자리(수동, 우울해진 상태) → depressed. those who are depressed = 우울한 사람들

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 심리학자는 하나의 원인(외로움)을 골라, 그 조건이 '우울증을 유발할(bring on a depression)' 수 있음을 입증하려 한다는 맥락이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① prevent all illness — 모든 병을 예방함 (원인 입증 흐름과 무관)
✅ ② bring on a depression — 우울증을 유발함 ←정답
❌ ③ explain every variation — 모든 변이를 설명함 (생물학자의 접근)
❌ ④ cure the loneliness — 외로움을 치료함 (문맥 무관)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그녀가 외롭다고 말할지라도, 대사 질환이라는 더 깊은 원인이 있으므로 그 외로움이 '우울한 기분의 주된 원인(the major cause of her melancholic mood)'은 아닐 수 있다는 맥락이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① a sign of her recovery — 회복의 신호 (문맥 무관)
❌ ② the only source of her joy — 기쁨의 유일한 원천 (우울과 반대)
✅ ③ the major cause of her melancholic mood — 우울한 기분의 주된 원인 ←정답
❌ ④ the reason for her recent success — 최근 성공의 이유 (문맥 무관)
det.tip: may not be the major cause = 주된 원인이 아닐 수 있다(더 깊은 생물학적 원인 존재)
